proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall the presently existing tax limitation of one-half (1/2) mil (one half dollar or 50 cents per $1,000.00 of taxable value) which may be assessed against all of the taxable property in the County of Ontonagon, State of Michigan, be renewed and continued for a period of four (4) years, 2027 through 2030, both inclusive, as provided by Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution, said taxes to be used by the Ontonagon County Commission on Aging for the maintenance and expansion of its programs for senior citizens and maintenance on its building.
Renewal will raise an estimated $189,752.93 in the first year the millage is levied.
proposals.officialTitle: Ontonagon County Commission on Aging Millage Renewal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of the levy described in the ballot language for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Ontonagon Area School District, Ontonagon County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars ($480,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor for the purpose of purchasing school buses?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is .42 mill ($0.42 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0 mill net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is five (5) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is .42 mill ($0.42 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: Ontonagon Area School District Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $480,000 in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.name: Copper Country Intermediate School District Special Education Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will replace millage that expires with the 2026 tax levy and will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy area special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in the Copper Country Intermediate School District, Michigan, be increased by 0.2903 mill ($0.2903 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 20 years, 2027 to 2046, inclusive, to provide funds…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will replace millage that expires with the 2026 tax levy and will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy area special education millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in the Copper Country Intermediate School District, Michigan, be increased by 0.2903 mill ($0.2903 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 20 years, 2027 to 2046, inclusive, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability; the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $601,033 from local property taxes authorized herein?
proposals.officialTitle: COPPER COUNTRY INTERMEDIATE SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL EDUCATION MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 0.2903 mills for 20 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Ontonagon Area School District, Ontonagon County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars ($480,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor for the purpose of purchasing school buses?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is .42 mill ($0.42 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0 mill net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is five (5) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is .42 mill ($0.42 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: Ontonagon Area School District Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $480,000 in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.name: Library Millage Proposition
proposals.description: Shall Stannard Township impose an increase of up to 0.25 mills ($0.25 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Artice IX, Sec. 6, of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030 inclusive, for the purpose of supporting McMillan Township Library services, which 0.25 mills increase will raise an estimated $6,468.00 in the first year the millage is levied to be disbursed to McMillan Township, Ontonagon County.
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall Stannard Township impose an increase of up to 0.25 mills ($0.25 per $1,000.00 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Artice IX, Sec. 6, of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four (4) years, 2027 through 2030 inclusive, for the purpose of supporting McMillan Township Library services, which 0.25 mills increase will raise an estimated $6,468.00 in the first year the millage is levied to be disbursed to McMillan Township, Ontonagon County.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 0.25 mills for 4 years — this is a tax increase.

proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.
